strategies.name: vwap_trend_continuation_retest
strategies.entry_summary: Form a directional bias first, then wait for price to extend away from VWAP to at least the first, preferably the second, standard-deviation band. After price breaks back through that band and retests it, enter in the original trend direction.
strategies.exit_summary: Use the higher outer standard-deviation bands as profit targets; the speaker specifically says the second and third standard deviations can be used as targets.

variants.variant_label: long continuation after reclaiming lower discount band
variants.timeframe_note: session-based intraday setup, especially around New York open
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to reach the first or second discount band, then break back above and retest before going long
variants.target_note: use the second and third standard deviations as targets
variants.transcript_quote: after we broke it and tested it we can try our long trade this can be one of the ways to use it and you can use the second and third standard deev atx

strategies.name: vwap_band_mean_reversion
strategies.entry_summary: When price reaches the outer VWAP standard-deviation bands, treat them as overbought/oversold extremes and look for a reversal entry from those stretched levels.
strategies.exit_summary: Target a move back to the central VWAP as the rebalance destination.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: use the outer VWAP bands as overbought or oversold levels for reversal trades
variants.target_note: central VWAP as target for price rebalancing
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels not just based on previous price but bas

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches two distinct runnable skeletons: a continuation setup using a break-and-retest after extension from VWAP, and an opposing mean-reversion setup from outer VWAP bands back to the central VWAP.
